_note: The ring on Outskirts (src/game/ring.ts). Apex runs six rounds; ours keep its shape and its damage per tick (3, 4, 10, 15, 20, 25 outside, one tick every 1.5 s) and scale the waits and the closes to a map 440 m across instead of a kilometre and a half (docs/GAP_ANALYSIS.md 4). Radii are ours, picked so round one still leaves most of the map playable and round six is a point.
_tick: seconds between damage ticks outside (Apex: 1.5 s)
_bounds: the battle royale's square, copied from BR_X, BR_Z and BR_HALF in src/game/br.ts. The ring reads them here rather than importing br.ts, which builds meshes on load. Every picked circle is drawn again until it sits wholly inside this square, up to `attempts` times: a circle whose edge ran past it stranded players in the void, because the player is hard-clamped to the same square (src/game/player.ts). Clamping instead of redrawing put the first circle's edge flush against the map edge in 58 matches in a hundred and on one of four identical corner points in another 9, because round one draws in a 157 m disc and the box is 80 m across; acceptance is about a third, so 24 tries fail about once in 10^11.
_cover: Late circles used to land on open sand as often as on a place, so the end game was a flat plain shoot-out. From `fromPhase` on the ring draws `candidates` centres the ordinary way and keeps the one with the best cover score, w * e^(-d / falloff) against the nearest attractor: a pull that falls by e every `falloff` metres, which is steep enough that cover underfoot beats a bigger place out of reach (a weight of 3 is worth about 27 m of walking over a weight of 1). Candidates are still random draws, so no two matches end on the same spot and no one place takes more than a third of them. Ours, swept in tools/checks/ring-place.ts: 8 draws and 25 m end nine matches in ten within 25 m of cover while still spreading over eleven of the map's twenty-one places.
_pace: How fast the ring pulls in, the lobby's own setting (src/ui/lobby.ts, the panel's "Ring" box). It multiplies every round's wait and close, so the circles and the damage are the same match at any pace and only the clock moves: `slow` is a long looting match, `fast` is the twelve-minute one. Resurgence's own scale (src/config/abilities-resurgence, resurgence.ts ringScale) multiplies on top of whichever is picked.
_attractors: Where the fights should end, in map-local metres (add the bounds centre for world space), each with a pull weight. The five big places from br.ts's poi list pull hardest, the four corner compounds next, and the twelve roadside stops (br.ts's ruins, culverts and container stacks) least: they are cover on the way, not somewhere to hold. tools/checks/ring-place.ts fails if these drift from br.ts.
